**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `fb87062f7ebcb6f850279923ecb683833dffa45f`.

Reviewed only `fb87062`, on top of the prior `a63edce` cost verdict. That verdict and its earlier request-list/body, awaited-drain, rename and live-proof limits stand. Closing adds no executable launch, polling loop, timer, Git/ddocs write or model wake.

| Surface | Cost and limits |
|---|---|
| Close admission | One keyed open-request read before writing. A recorded holder skips the broader withdrawal-authority helper; the requester also has a short path. Other authorized actors can pay existing project-assignment history, all-project, designated-prime and role-list reads. These are command-local inventory reads, not a new background query loop. Arguments/why and the full stored request are materialized; cost is not just one scalar lookup. |
| Move to closed history | `role_requests.rs:765-817` reuses the existing owned-write primitive: one transaction, keyed `INSERT ... SELECT` for the requested state, then keyed DELETE on a successful move. Completion reads the closed row, or falls back to the open row when no move occurred. Wrong-state attempts can still enter a no-row move transaction before returning the refusal. Already-closed replay is detected before the handler attempts another move. |
| Time-limit work | Successful delivered closure removes the open row from the existing limit pass, so future rounds no longer probe that request. It adds no cancellation sweep or new clock. Queued self-request closure in the drain still uses the same helper with `from = queued`; its task/transaction budget is unchanged. |
| Notification | Quiet and requester-self closes skip notification. Otherwise a successful close uses one best-effort `hold_fyi`, including existing recipient/permission/queue work; it never opens a model turn. “One close write” is not one total transaction when the FYI is held too. Its stable message ID dedupes notification. A failed hold is reported in the receipt after closure; there is no background retry, and replay adds no second notification attempt. |
| Closed row/schema | The unmerged 0037 table gains nullable holder and delivered-at fields, copied by the same move. This adds metadata bytes, not a row-rebuild loop or new index. Original bodies remain retained in closed history and are read into full records even though listing/close metadata does not expose them. No forward ALTER/backfill operation for an already-applied older 0037 is added by this delta; reviewer owns that compatibility question. |

No new whole-operation latency or body-size cap is introduced. Nonquiet response latency includes its post-commit FYI attempt; privileged authority checks may depend on inventory/history size.

**CI proof:** GitHub is CLEAN at this exact head. [CI 42372442784](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42372442784) has all four jobs successful, and latest [delivers 42372724688](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42372724688) succeeds. Rust JUnit records **2,068 executed cases, zero failures/errors**, including delivered-close/limit-stop/quiet behavior, prior queued withdrawal/self-close behavior and all six spawn guards. Five Rust tests were skipped separately.

No local builds, tests, mutation runs, runtime probes or review-tree edits. Cost verdict only; reviewer/security own delivered-state authority, replay and migration compatibility closure.

**Still owed:** prior matched deployment launch-rate and CPU/RSS readings, with PID/build, actual elapsed time and workload; contended close/drain/rename latency remains unmeasured. Migration renumbering on rebase remains required if a higher-numbered migration merges first.
